title: The Omniscience of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The omniscience of God means that God knows all things perfectly. He knows the past, present, future, creation, history, every heart, every motive, and every hidden thing.
summary: The omniscience of God means that God knows all things perfectly. He knows the past, present, future, creation, history, every heart, every motive, and every hidden thing.
christFocus: Jesus Christ knows His sheep, searches hearts, and reveals the Father’s perfect knowledge. In Him, believers are fully known and yet graciously called, kept, and loved.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s knowledge is complete. He does not learn, guess, discover, or overlook. All things are open before Him, and nothing in creation is hidden from His sight.

God knows not only actions, but hearts and motives. He knows thoughts before they are spoken, needs before they are expressed, and sins that people try to bury. His knowledge is perfect and personal.

God also knows the end from the beginning. The future is not uncertain to Him. His knowledge is joined with His wisdom, sovereignty, and purpose, so history does not surprise Him.

For those in Christ, being fully known is not only sobering but comforting. The God who knows the worst about His people also knows their weakness, grief, longing, and need for mercy.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often live as though they are unseen or misunderstood. Some hide sin, while others feel their pain is invisible. God’s omniscience confronts both lies: nothing is hidden, and nothing is unnoticed.

This doctrine gives honesty and comfort. Believers do not have to pretend before God. He already knows, and in Christ He invites His people to come into the light.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live honestly before the God who knows you completely. Confess hidden sin, bring Him your anxieties, and trust His care over details you cannot see. Let His perfect knowledge lead you away from hypocrisy and into humble confidence in Christ.
